question: Which LLTO coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, how does it compare with the pristine NCM, and why did the 2 mol.% coating lower the rate capability?

rendered:
The LLTO coating that retained the most capacity after 200 cycles[1] at 0.5C[2] was the coating labelled LLTO-2, the 2 mol.%[3] coating, which kept 86.2%[4] of its initial discharge capacity. The pristine NCM kept only 56.6%[5] of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles[6], so the LLTO-2 coating retained far more capacity than the bare material. LLTO-0.5 kept 85.5%[7] and LLTO-1 kept 57.2%[8], which is only slightly above the pristine NCM.
On rate capability, the paper says the coated NCM improved, but with the 2 mol.% coating[9] the rate capability decreased. The authors suggest this may be due to the increase in the thickness of the coating layer, which suppresses the electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling. This is offered as a possible explanation, not a verified explanation. The same coating gave the best cycling retention.[10][11]
